valuation_philosophy.model_type: Blended AFFO-capitalization / NTA-based cost-of-equity model (REIT), NOT a WACC-based owner-FCF DCF
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Precinct is an internally managed, levered NZX premium CBD office REIT (stapled security: PPNZ property owner + PPIL manager). Reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised IAS 40 investment-property revaluations (+$254.9m FY2018, -$153.1m FY2023, -$22.1m FY2024) and is not a cash-flow proxy; statutory EPS and P/E are noise and are excluded as drivers. The CSV FreeCashFlow column is structurally negative in nearly every period (-$353.7m FY2021, -$139.6m FY2023) because development capex (Commercial Bay, Bowen Campus, Molesworth Street, Downtown Car Park, 256 Queen Street student accommodation) runs through investing cash flow -- that is growth capital, not maintenance, and using OCF-less-capex as the base would value the company as if every development dollar were a cost of running the existing portfolio. The valuation base is company-disclosed AFFO per stapled security (FFO less maintenance capex and incentives), which is measured AFTER interest expense -- an equity-level cash flow. It is therefore capitalized at the COST OF EQUITY, never a blended WACC, and net debt ($1,503m at 31-Dec-2025) is NEVER subtracted from the resulting value: the debt cost is already inside AFFO, and deducting it again is the classic REIT double-count. The final value blends 50/50: (1) capitalized AFFO at cost of equity with an exit-AFFO-yield terminal value (capped multiple, no runaway Gordon growth), and (2) PV of interim cash dividends plus projected NTA per security at a justified exit P/NTA -- appropriate because Precinct, unlike its NZX REIT peers, traded AT or ABOVE NTA for most of the last decade (FY-end P/NTA 0.92-1.21x FY2017-FY2025, average ~1.02x) and now sits at 0.87x. J-CURVE HANDLING OF THE $325m RAISE: the Oct/Nov-2025 equity raise lifted securities 1,587.0m to 1,852.8m (+16.8%) and diluted H1 FY2026 AFFO to 2.76 cps (from 3.23 cps). That capital funds ASB North Wharf (via PPILP), the 1,602-bed student accommodation pipeline and Downtown Car Park -- raised but not yet earning. The base case neither annualises the diluted H1 run-rate into perpetuity (which would assume the $325m earns nothing, ever) nor grants an immediate stabilised yield: FY2026 AFFO is anchored at 6.40 cps (H1 actual 2.76 + a management-guided H2 skew from Molesworth Street completion, lower funding costs and student-accommodation revenue recognition, at ~88% AFFO/FFO conversion against the 7.30-7.50 cps FFO guidance), then recovers +1.5% in FY2027 (capital still deploying, PwC Tower 50% sell-down to PAG settling H1 FY27 shrinks the rental base but adds fees and cuts debt) and +3.0%/yr in FY2028-29 as deployed capital contributes, fading to +2.0% terminal. PAYOUT SUSTAINABILITY is central: the 6.75 cps dividend has EXCEEDED AFFO in every year since FY2021 (AFFO payout 100-103%; 111% of TTM AFFO of 6.07 cps). The company targets ~90-92% of FFO, but on a post-maintenance-capex basis the distribution is part-funded by asset recycling and debt. Base case therefore holds the dividend flat at 6.75 cps for five years (no growth until AFFO coverage is restored ~FY2029); bear case cuts it to 5.5 cps. The blended base value of ~$0.94 sits below the $1.03 price -- a mature income vehicle at the bottom of its 10-year price range, roughly fairly valued for yield with the imminent FY2026 result (27-Aug-2026) the near-term swing factor.

warnings: FY2026 full-year result is due 27-Aug-2026 -- three days after this valuation. The FY2026 AFFO anchor (base 6.40 cps) is an estimate against 7.30-7.50 cps FFO guidance with a large guided H2 skew (H1 FFO was only 3.18 cps); the actual print is the single biggest near-term swing factor and this DCF should be refreshed against it.

The 6.75 cps dividend has exceeded AFFO every year since FY2021 (103% of FY2025 AFFO, 111% of TTM AFFO 6.07 cps). The payout is covered ~91% against FFO but NOT against AFFO -- the post-maintenance-capex shortfall is funded by asset recycling and debt. Base case holds the DPS flat with zero growth; bear case models a cut to 5.5 cps.

AFFO per security is FLAT over five years (6.48 -> 6.54 cps FY2021-FY2025) despite $2.6bn+ of development since 2017 -- growth capital has so far only offset dilution and higher funding costs. selected_growth_rate is 0.23%/yr; the base-case forward recovery to ~7.2 cps by FY2031 rests on the $325m raise deploying productively, not on historical evidence of per-security compounding.

This is a REIT AFFO-capitalization + NTA model, not an owner-FCF DCF. Reported FreeCashFlow (structurally negative from development capex) and NetIncome (fair-value revaluation noise, +$254.9m FY2018 to -$153.1m FY2023) are excluded as drivers by design.
AFFO is already post-interest (equity-level). Net debt ($1,503.1m at 31-Dec-2025) is NEVER subtracted from the capitalized value -- doing so would double-count leverage embedded in the earnings base.

Wellington government-tenant exposure is a live headwind: core public service targeted to shrink ~14% by July 2029 and ~172,000 sqm of Wellington government leases expire 2026-2028 against Precinct's ~25-30% Wellington weighting (Bowen Campus, Defence House). Management itself calls Wellington 'more challenging'.

Rate direction has REVERSED: RBNZ raised the OCR to 2.50% in July 2026 (first hike since May 2023) with further hikes flagged -- a headwind to cap rates, to Precinct's floating-rate (BKBM-priced) debt with only ~2.8yr weighted average maturity, and to the NTA-leg exit multiples.

The PwC Tower 50:50 JV with PAG ($600m headline, largest single-asset Auckland CBD office deal) settles H1 FY27 subject to OIO approval -- deal risk until cleared. Capital-partnering (GIC/PPILP, PAG) is the funding flywheel; a pullback in offshore institutional appetite would stall de-gearing and growth.

PCTHB/PCTHC convertible notes had conversion-price caps reset by the $325m raise -- a contingent dilution source not in the flat 1,852.8m share-count assumption; treated as a bear-tail rather than modelled.

Terminal value is 66-75% of the AFFO-leg value across scenarios -- normal for a capitalization model but the valuation is correspondingly sensitive to the exit-yield / cost-of-equity assumptions (see sensitivity matrix).

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,852.8m stapled securities on issue at 31-Dec-2025 (H1 FY2026 balance sheet), post the Oct/Nov-2025 $325m raise (1,587.0m -> 1,852.8m, +16.8%). Held FLAT across the projection: no buybacks (verified $0 FY2023-H1 FY2026), no further raise assumed in base; PCTHB/PCTHC convertible-note dilution flagged as bear-tail, not modelled.
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt 1,528.7 less cash 25.6 at 31-Dec-2025 (H1 FY2026). NOT subtracted anywhere in this valuation -- AFFO is already post-interest; recorded for audit only. Pro forma gearing 33.7% after hotel/22 Stanley St proceeds repaid debt.
inputs.affo_ttm_note: TTM = FY2025 6.54 + H1 FY2026 2.76 - H1 FY2025 3.23 = 6.07 cps (NZX half-yearly reconstruction). Depressed by the equity raise: capital in the count, earnings not yet.
inputs.sbc_source: H1 FY2026 Metrics CSV (StockBasedComp, NZ$m). Immaterial (~0.1% of revenue) and already inside FFO/AFFO as an expense -- no separate adjustment needed for an AFFO-capitalization model; stated rather than silently skipped.
inputs.last_fcf_note: No owner-FCF figure is used -- reported FCF is structurally negative from development capex (growth capital, not maintenance). AFFO per stapled security is the valuation base, capitalized at cost of equity. See valuation_philosophy.
inputs.gearing_note: Pro forma 33.7% at 31-Dec-2025 after hotel/22 Stanley Street sale proceeds repaid debt; balance-sheet LVR was 41.6% at FY2025. Weighted average debt maturity only ~2.8 years.
inputs.model: REIT blended AFFO-capitalization + NTA leg (50/50), per dcf-methods routing table and ARG.NZ/IPL.NZ/NZL.NZ precedent
inputs.notes: Model: AFFO/NTA blend at cost of equity -- routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT row; owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here (FCF structurally negative from development capex, NetIncome is revaluation noise, EBITDA undefined under IAS 40). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Price NZ$1.03 is the 21-Aug-2026 NZX close (Yahoo regularMarketTime 2026-08-21T04:59:51Z; no trade yet on 24-Aug at fetch time -- normal weekend gap, not a stale/delisted quote). FY2026 result due 27-Aug-2026 is the imminent catalyst.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: AFFO per stapled security 4yr CAGR FY2021-FY2025 (6.48 -> 6.54 cps) -- essentially flat; stored as a percent for the screener
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total AFFO grew 5.0%/yr (85.3 -> 103.8 NZ$m) while AFFO PER SECURITY grew 0.23%/yr -- the entire gap is share issuance funding development (1,458.5m -> 1,587.0m securities FY2021-FY2025, now 1,852.8m). Revenue CAGR (11.9%) is grosser still and includes hotels since sold. Per-share AFFO, not totals, is the honest driver for a serially-issuing REIT.
historical_growth.notes: Standard revenue/EPS/equity CAGR selection does not apply: NetIncome and book equity swing on unrealised cap-rate revaluations (NTA $1.54 FY2022 -> $1.18 H1 FY2026), and reported FCF is structurally negative from development capex. AFFO per security has been range-bound 6.48-6.69 cents for five years -- the central fact the base case is built around: forward growth comes from deploying the $325m raise, Auckland rent reversion (10.3% contract rent growth 1H26) and capital-partnering fees, not from any demonstrated per-security compounding.

cost_of_equity_build.risk_free_rate_note: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5-4.7%; RBNZ raised the OCR to 2.50% in July 2026 (first hike since May 2023) with further hikes flagged into Sep/Oct-2026 -- the long end is biased up, not down
cost_of_equity_build.beta_note: NZ listed-property beta below 1.0 (contracted rent, 97% occupancy, 6.1yr WALT, blue-chip/government covenants) but elevated by 33.7% pro forma gearing and pure-play office concentration versus diversified peers
cost_of_equity_build.office_structural_premium_note: Only NZX-listed pure-play premium CBD office REIT -- carries hybrid-work/structural office demand risk its diversified peers (KPG retail-mixed, GMT industrial, ARG 52% industrial, IPL large-format retail) do not; flight-to-quality is currently a tailwind but the aggregate-demand overhang is multi-year
cost_of_equity_build.wellington_government_premium_note: ~25-30% Wellington weighting against a public service targeted to shrink ~14% by July 2029, with ~172,000 sqm of government leases expiring 2026-2028
cost_of_equity_build.development_execution_premium_note: Downtown Car Park is a very large, multi-year, capital-hungry redevelopment still in consenting with only ~50% of office NLA in pre-commitment talks; 1,602-bed student accommodation pipeline runs concurrently
cost_of_equity_build.gearing_refinancing_premium_note: Pro forma 33.7% LVR is mid-band and the Aug-2025 refinance ($268m into 2030 facilities) shows market access; the ~2.8yr weighted debt maturity is captured in beta and the bear scenario rather than double-charged here
cost_of_equity_build.illiquidity_premium_note: NZ$1.9bn market cap, S&P/NZX 20 constituent -- no small-cap illiquidity premium (unlike IPL.NZ)
cost_of_equity_build.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY, not WACC -- AFFO is post-interest so debt cost is already in the flow. Built in NZD off the NZ risk-free rate, matching the NZD flows and NZD quote (no currency mismatch). Base 10.25% = CAPM 9.4% (rf 4.6% + 0.80 x 6.0% ERP) + 0.35% office-structural + 0.25% Wellington-government + 0.25% development-execution. Bull 9.5% assumes the easing cycle resumes and flight-to-quality persists; bear 11.5% prices renewed hikes plus Wellington stress. Deliberately NOT a generic 8%: a levered, single-sector office landlord in a rate-hiking environment must clear materially more than its 6.55% dividend yield.

base.rationale: FY2026 anchor 6.40 cps AFFO (H1 actual 2.76 + guided H2 skew: Molesworth Street PC Jan-2026 with MFAT as largest tenant, funding costs down 5.20% -> 4.41%, ASB North Wharf income via PPILP from May-2026, student-accommodation revenue recognition, Investment Boost; ~88% AFFO/FFO conversion vs 7.30-7.50 cps FFO guidance -- i.e. FFO delivered near the LOW end). J-curve: +1.5% FY2027 (raise capital still deploying; PwC Tower 50% sell-down to PAG settles H1 FY27, shrinking rent base but adding management fees and cutting debt), +3.0% FY2028-29 as deployed capital contributes, +2.5%/+2.0% thereafter -- recovery to ~7.2 cps by FY2031, i.e. five years to earn back the dilution. Dividend HELD FLAT at 6.75 cps (AFFO does not cover it until ~FY2029; no growth assumed). NTA +1.0%/yr (broadly stable cap rates, PwC JV at book, modest development margin). Exit AFFO yield 6.5% (15.4x) -- conservative against the 17-25x Precinct actually traded FY2021-25 -- and exit P/NTA 0.90x vs a 10yr FY-end average of ~1.02x: partial, not full, closure of the current 0.87x discount.

bull.rationale: FY2026 FFO prints at guidance mid-to-top (AFFO 6.60 cps); RBNZ hiking scare passes and easing resumes; Auckland flight-to-quality reversion (10.3% contract rent growth 1H26) captured across the book; Downtown Car Park reaches Stage-1 commitment ~Q4 CY2026 largely pre-let and part-funded by capital partners; PAG/GIC flywheel scales toward the $4-5bn partnerships target, growing fee income. AFFO recovers past 6.9 cps by FY2028 and ~8.0 by FY2031; dividend resumes growth as coverage is restored; NTA +2.5%/yr with cap-rate compression; exit P/NTA 1.05x (within the 0.99-1.21x FY2019-21 range) and exit AFFO yield 5.75% (17.4x, still below the FY2021-23 traded 20-25x).

bear.rationale: FY2026 misses guidance (AFFO 6.10 cps); RBNZ keeps hiking, stalling cap-rate recovery and repricing the BKBM-linked debt stack (2.8yr maturity runway); Wellington government downsizing bites -- non-renewals across the 172,000 sqm of 2026-28 expiries hit Bowen Campus/Defence House occupancy; Downtown Car Park cost overruns or a failed Stage-1 commitment; OIO delays or breaks the PAG settlement, stalling de-gearing. AFFO sags to ~5.9 cps and the uncovered 6.75 cps dividend is cut to 5.5 cps (≈94% of AFFO) from FY2028. NTA -2.5%/yr (a smaller-scale repeat of the FY2023-25 devaluation cycle) and the P/NTA discount persists at 0.75x; exit AFFO yield 7.5% (13.3x).

base.note: No net-debt deduction: AFFO is an equity-level, post-interest flow

nta_based_leg.methodology: PV of interim cash dividends at cost of equity + PV of exit value (year-5 NTA per security x justified exit P/NTA). No net-debt deduction -- NTA is already post-debt equity book value.

cross_checks.floor_basis: FY2026e AFFO 6.40 cps capitalized in perpetuity at 10.25% cost of equity, zero growth ever
cross_checks.nta_anchor_basis: 31-Dec-2025 NTA. Precinct's 10yr FY-end P/NTA averaged ~1.02x (range 0.87-1.21x) -- unlike diversified NZX REIT peers it has NOT persistently traded at a discount, so NTA is a genuine central anchor here, not just a ceiling. Base blended IV of ~$0.94 implies 0.80x -- below the current 0.87x and below anything in the 10yr history, i.e. conservative.
cross_checks.implied_cap_rate_basis: Market P/NTA of 0.873x prices attributable equity ~NZ$278m below book; loading that discount onto the ~NZ$3.0bn investment portfolio implies ~6.4% vs the 5.8% book weighted average cap rate -- the market is already pricing ~60bp of cap-rate expansion.

entry_price.basis: AFFO-capitalization leg only (base case), consistent with the skill formula (post-2026-07-21 fix, IPL.NZ template). Interim AFFO and the exit terminal value discounted at the 15% hurdle; TV computed at the base-case 6.5% exit AFFO yield (what a buyer pays at exit). No net-debt adjustment -- AFFO is already post-interest.

sensitivity.matrix_note: AFFO-capitalization leg only, base AFFO path held constant. Rows = cost of equity (8.25%-12.25%), columns = exit AFFO yield (5.5%-7.5%). NZD per security.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 50/25/25. Base at 50%: guidance was reaffirmed at H1 with named H2 drivers, Auckland leasing momentum is verifiable (10.3% contract rent growth, >25,000 sqm leased), and the PAG/GIC partnerships are signed. Bear kept at a full 25% (not the house-default 15%): the FY2026 result lands in three days against an ambitious H2 skew, the RBNZ has resumed HIKING, the dividend is uncovered against AFFO, and Wellington government downsizing is a quantified, dated headwind. Bull 25%: the flight-to-quality reversion and capital-partnering flywheel are real but already partly in the price.

sanity_check.note: REIT model: multiples use company-disclosed AFFO/FFO per stapled security and NTA, not GAAP EPS or EBITDA. P/E is skipped (statutory EPS swings on unrealised IAS 40 revaluations: +$254.9m FY2018, -$153.1m FY2023) and EV/EBITDA is skipped (no clean D&A/EBIT split under fair-value accounting; EBITDA deliberately NULL in the Metrics CSV). The REIT-meaningful multiples -- P/NTA, P/AFFO (AFFO yield) and implied cap rate -- are checked against Precinct's own 10-year traded history (June FY-end closes from Yahoo 10y monthly series vs FY NTA/AFFO from kpis).

price_range_10yr.current_position: at the bottom of the range (current $1.03 vs 10yr low $1.025)

implied_multiples_at_current_price.p_e_note: Skipped: statutory EPS is fair-value-revaluation noise for a REIT
implied_multiples_at_current_price.ev_ebitda_note: Skipped: EBITDA structurally undefined under IAS 40; NULL in Metrics CSV by design

historical_averages_10yr.p_nta_note: Unlike ARG/IPL, Precinct traded AT OR ABOVE NTA for most of the decade (0.92-1.21x FY2017-FY2025); the current 0.87x is the cheapest P/NTA in its listed history -- the market is pricing office-sector structural risk and the uncovered dividend, not a peer-normal REIT discount
historical_averages_10yr.p_affo_note: P/AFFO 18.1-24.7x FY2021-25 at June FY-end closes; inflated by the low-rate era -- the model's 15.4x base exit multiple sits well below the entire traded range

trip_thresholds.upside_trip: upside >100% while price sits in the upper half of the 10yr range -- N/A: price is at the BOTTOM of the range and base-case upside is negative

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Base blended IV $0.94 implies 0.80x P/NTA -- below the current price's own 0.87x, below every FY-end observation in the 10-year history (min 0.87x), and far below the 1.82x trip line. Implied P/AFFO at base IV (14.7x on FY2026e) is below the current price's 17.0x TTM and the bottom of the 18.1-24.7x traded range, far below the 40.9x trip line. The model is conservative relative to history by construction: base exit P/NTA (0.90x) sits below the 1.02x decade average, the exit AFFO multiple (15.4x) below the entire traded range, the dividend is held flat because AFFO does not cover it, and the current price is at its 10-year low so the peak-extrapolation trip cannot apply. Negative base-case upside (-8.9%) at the bottom of the price range is a legitimate 'fairly valued for yield, uncovered distribution' conclusion, not a model artifact.
sanity_check.fix_note: No fix needed -- no threshold tripped on first pass.
